column1: # P/02 implementation stages: one possible plan, not a behavior norm.
# The installer is one-shot, with no HTTP door: no door or launch stage. The prior P/01 stand is available for puts and rights.
# gate is a semicolon-separated conjunction: verdicts:<chapter>:<case,...|*>, puts:<chapter>:<case,...|*>,
# verdicts/puts/accept select their own published table and judge; * is the full target including its published variants.
# seams selects scenarios of the seams.tsv of the chapter, run through the seam adapter (common acceptance README); the other checks keep their own judge.
# code:* — the rows of forms/code-rules.tsv whose stage is this stage or a stage of a smaller n hold, under the closed dictionary of the code
# checks Platform/common/acceptance/forms/code-rules.tsv; the generation cycle checks them, not the acceptance; * is
# the only argument; a row is a data error when neither its stage nor a stage of a larger n has code:* in its gate.
# n is consecutive; depends names earlier n; weight is 1..5.
# - means none. Empty when means always applicable.
# The checklist retains the proof of units, install/upgrade, environment, TLS, CA, clients, the OS and real rollout/barriers.
# build confirms build only; the pure poll seams do not execute a rollout. Domain references in loader/rights remain whole inputs.
# norms — elements separated by «; »: the sections of the norms, the forms and the packages the stage builds on, and the items of the readiness
# checklists of spec/*.norms.md (the lines - [ ] **P/02.K-MM**), written P/02.K-MM; each item stands in the norms of exactly one stage, the stage at
# which every subject of the item exists; an item at no stage or at two stages is a data error. The items of the system
# checklists of spec/*.norms.md stand at no stage: they need the OS, a host or several lessons.
